references.text: The parable of the sower in Isaiah illustrates how God's word can be choked by worries and wealth, similar to how thorns choke the word in Mark 4:18.
In Matthew's version of the parable of the sower, it is also mentioned how worldly anxieties and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word.
Luke provides a parallel to Mark 4:18, explaining how life's worries, wealth, and pleasures choke the word.
Hebrews 6:7-8 uses a similar image of land that bears thorns and thistles, which is worthless and near to being cursed, which can be seen as a spiritual parallel to Mark 4:18.
James speaks about how desire, when it has conceived, gives birth to sin, and sin, when it is fully grown, brings forth death, which relates to how the word is choked in Mark 4:18.
In Revelation, there is talk of holding fast to the word despite trials, which can be seen in contrast to those who let the word be choked as in Mark 4:18.
